QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_56

question.text: In the Niwas case under SAS-1100, the "income uplift" type of indicator is challenging because:

answer.text: Income uplift is not relevant to the SAS-1100 housing context
Income is not measurable in any form

Beneficiaries were not willing to share income, savings and other financial indicators, so the SIA must work with what is available and disclose the limitation, while drawing on related source-listed metrics such as reduced repair expenses and savings
The SIA is prohibited from asking financial questions

explanation.text: The Logic: The Niwas pages support family income, savings and repair-expense indicators and explicitly note that beneficiaries were not willing to share income, savings and other financial indicators. The SIA's task is to acknowledge this reluctance, work with the indicators that are available, and disclose the limitation in the report. The Trap: Income uplift is part of the Niwas indicator set (A is wrong), income can be measured indirectly (B is wrong), and the workbook does not prohibit the SIA from asking financial questions (D is wrong). Note: Where direct income data is not forthcoming, anchor the assessment to source-listed indicators such as savings and reduced repair expenses, and disclose the data-availability limitation transparently.
